keyIdea:
Order the data. The median $Q_2$ splits it into two halves; the **lower quartile** $Q_1$ is the median of the lower half and the **upper quartile** $Q_3$ is the median of the upper half (for odd $n$, leave the median out of both halves). For GCSE you may also use positions $\frac{n+1}{4}$ and $\frac{3(n+1)}{4}$.

**Interquartile range**: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$, the spread of the middle 50%, not affected by extreme values.

**Five-number summary**: minimum, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, maximum. A **box plot** draws the box from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ with a line at the median, and whiskers out to the smallest and largest values. Each of the four sections holds about 25% of the data, however long it is.

**Outliers**: a value is an outlier if it is below $Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$. Plot it as a separate cross and end the whisker at the most extreme value that is not an outlier.

**Data cleaning**: before analysing, leave out missing values (and say how many), and correct obvious errors when the intended value is clear (e.g. 1.65 m typed instead of 165 cm) or remove them if not. Only remove an outlier if it is an error or not from the population; a genuine extreme value stays in.
